name: auto-ontology
description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
one_liner: A library that builds a 'business dictionary' for a company's data, so an AI assistant knows what a term like 'revenue' actually means before it answers a question about it.
buyer: A data platform lead at a mid-size company whose execs have stopped trusting the AI chatbot's numbers because it keeps pulling the wrong definition of a metric.
business_use_cases: A data consultancy sells an 'ontology audit' engagement: map a client's messy warehouse into one trusted set of definitions so their AI dashboards stop contradicting each other.
A vertical AI startup (finance, healthcare ops) uses it as the grounding layer behind a 'trustworthy analytics copilot' it sells to enterprises, citing sources on every answer.
A BI/analytics vendor bolts it on as a governance add-on so customers can prove, in an audit, exactly where an AI-generated number came from.

money_ideas.idea: Enterprise subscription for hosting and maintaining a client's ontology as their data and definitions evolve.
One-off consulting engagement to build the initial ontology and wire it into an existing BI stack.

steal_this: Pick one public dataset (e.g. a city's open-data budget spreadsheets) and build a weekend demo: 'ask the budget questions, get a cited, provably-correct answer' — a good sales demo for the audit-consulting pitch above.
